newsitem.title: INDIA: India says Saudis deported boy beggars.
newsitem.headline: India says Saudis deported boy beggars.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has deported 47 Indian boys aged between seven and 13 after they were caught begging, Indian police and officials said on Monday.
"A group of 47 boys has arrived by a Saudi Arabia Airlines flight this evening," an airport police official told Reuters.
The boys were being held by police prior to being sent to a remand home where they would stay until police could trace their relatives, he said.
It was the second group of children deported this year by Saudi Arabia, known for its tough immigration laws. A group of 76 girls, many of them handicapped, had arrived on January 14.
Most of the boys were the children of migrants who stayed on in Saudi Arabia after their visas expired and had since been deported, the police official said.
"I did not go to Saudi Arabia to beg. I went with my father and we sold caps to the pilgrims. But I got separated and left behind," eight-year-old Usnan told Reuters at Bombay's airport.
"I went to Saudi Arabia with my father. He suddenly disappeared one day, leaving me to fend for myself," said a boy named Babu who did not give his age.
All of the boys came from Murshidabad town in the eastern state of West Bengal, authorities said.
"We will make arrangements to give them a meal before we take them to the remand home," the official said. The home for juveniles is located in central Bombay's crowded Dongri area.
